title: Widest-Path Reachability Fields for Connectivity-Preserving Slender Structure Segmentation
mechanism: A differentiable max-min (widest path) reachability objective on a domain-restricted graph sends gradient to the sparse bottleneck pixels that break connectivity. No inference overhead.
adaptation: Domain = crack label dilated by 2 px to absorb jitter, endpoints from the label skeleton, DP on GPU. An alternative solver to TRACE for the same goal, so pick one.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + WPRF (crack), 5 seeds. Baseline: PF. Metrics: component recall, relF1@2, crack IoU, width. Kill as for TRACE.
evidence: R (abstract): 9 architectures, 6 datasets including cracks. Improved 87% of experiments with fixed hyperparameters, clDice +7.2 points on fragile datasets.

alt_notes.adaptation: Domain = crack label dilated by 2 px (absorbs jitter); endpoints from the label skeleton. Same aim as TRACE with a global solver; run only if TRACE shows a gain.
alt_notes.min_experiment: PF + WPRF vs PF, 5 seeds. Kill if relF1@2 gain < 0.01 or width rises > 15%.
